item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The Committee noted that Egypt submitted its fifth periodic report 19 years late, although it engaged in constructive dialogue and provided written replies to the Committee's questions.","question_ids":["7B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The finding was adopted in November 2023 and concerns Egypt's reporting and engagement over the review period; it does not establish a personal act by el-Sisi.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee assessed the Egyptian State party; attribution to el-Sisi is indirect through executive-state responsibility.","limitations":["The supplied text does not identify which actions were personally directed by el-Sisi."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":5,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The Committee welcomed Egypt's ratification or accession to several human-rights and anti-trafficking instruments and cited legislation and institutions concerning women, persons with disabilities, migrants, prisoners, psychiatric patients, torture victims and human rights.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.4","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The Committee recorded measures adopted before and during the period reviewed in its 2023 observations.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern state institutions under el-Sisi's presidency but do not establish his personal authorship of each measure.","limitations":["The document does not provide implementation outcomes for every listed measure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that Egypt lacked information on how conflicts between domestic law and the Convention were resolved and had provided no examples of domestic courts directly invoking or applying the Convention.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.4","7B.6","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was made in the Committee's 2023 review of Egypt's implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egypt's legal and judicial system; it does not prove a personal decision by el-Sisi.","limitations":["The observation is about missing examples and information, not a quantified rate of non-application."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that Egypt's statutory definition of torture was not fully aligned with the Convention: it did not cover all intentional severe physical or mental suffering, official consent or acquiescence, attempted torture, complicity or participation, and did not clearly recognize superior responsibility or an absolute non-derogable prohibition.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","7B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Committee made this legal finding in 2023 concerning the domestic framework in force during the review period.","ruler_attribution":"This is an institutional finding about Egyptian law under el-Sisi's government, not a finding of his personal conduct.","limitations":["The supplied text reports legal deficiencies and recommendations, not a personal order by el-Sisi."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported that broad counter-terrorism laws were used to silence actual or perceived government critics; terrorism suspects could be held in police custody for up to 28 days and were reportedly held longer without charge, with allegations of arbitrary arrest, torture, ill-treatment, enforced disappearance and unfair proceedings.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","6B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Committee's 2023 observations describe practices and laws relevant to the period under review, while noting some measures dated from 2015-2021.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns government and security institutions during el-Sisi's presidency; it does not establish his personal involvement in each case.","limitations":["The text uses reported allegations and does not provide a complete case-level dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The Committee noted that Egypt lifted its state of emergency in October 2021 but remained concerned about far-reaching powers under the 1958 Emergency Act and COVID-19 amendments that expanded military-court jurisdiction over civilians and security-force detention powers with limited judicial oversight.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.4","4B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The institutional finding was issued in 2023 and concerns legal powers continuing into the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns the legal framework maintained by the Egyptian state under el-Sisi; it does not identify a personal 2023 directive.","limitations":["The text does not state that the state of emergency itself remained in force in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The Committee found reported widespread incommunicado detention and a rising trend in enforced disappearances, including cases in which courts ordered release, while official data and investigation information were unavailable.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was issued in 2023 regarding the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian detention and investigative authorities under el-Sisi's government; personal presidential direction is not shown.","limitations":["The Committee described reports and missing official data rather than providing a verified national count."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":12,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported that detainees were not routinely given arrest reasons or rights, lawyer access and independent medical examinations were not guaranteed, family notification was delayed or denied, detention registers were inconsistently used, presentation before a competent authority often exceeded the 24-hour limit, and challenges to detention legality were often not respected.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","6B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Committee recorded these reported practices in its 2023 observations of the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian law-enforcement, prosecutorial and judicial practice during el-Sisi's presidency; it is not a personal attribution.","limitations":["The document does not quantify the frequency of each reported practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported widespread prolonged pretrial detention, especially of government critics, and regular circumvention of statutory limits through 'rotation'—new detention orders based on similar charges after release orders—contributing to prison overcrowding; public detention totals were unavailable.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","6B.2","6B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was adopted in 2023 and concerns detention practices during the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns prosecutors and security agencies under el-Sisi's government; it does not prove his personal instruction.","limitations":["The source characterizes the practice as reported and gives no national total."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The Committee noted official steps to close substandard detention centres and construct additional facilities, but reported overcrowding, poor hygiene, inadequate ventilation, insufficient food and water, limited rehabilitation activities, inadequate health care, insufficient qualified prison staff, violence by prison staff, harsh conditions for political detainees and continued suspension of in-person visits in some facilities.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The 2023 observations acknowledge state infrastructure measures while describing conditions during the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The Committee assessed state detention administration under el-Sisi's presidency, without attributing each condition or improvement personally to him.","limitations":["The document provides no comprehensive outcome measure for the facility upgrades."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":18,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that reports described unlawful and incommunicado detention in unknown locations despite the state's assertion that Egypt had no secret detention places.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","7B.1","7B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This was a 2023 institutional finding concerning the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns the Egyptian state under el-Sisi; it does not establish that he personally made or knew the assertion.","limitations":["The source reports conflicting state and external accounts without resolving every alleged location."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":18,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported recurrent allegations that excessive force during protests caused deaths and injuries to hundreds of peaceful protesters, including children, and was accompanied by arbitrary arrest, incommunicado detention, torture and enforced disappearance; it also found inadequate accountability and a legal framework not aligned with international standards.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Committee issued this finding in 2023 concerning the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns security forces and the state framework under el-Sisi's presidency; personal authorization by el-Sisi is not established.","limitations":["The text says 'hundreds' and reports allegations rather than supplying a verified casualty register."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":21,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"The Committee found extended and increasing use of military courts against civilians under broad counter-terrorism and other laws, with many critics and political opponents, including children, tried and convicted in proceedings lacking due process and fair-trial guarantees.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","6B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was adopted in 2023 and concerns the period under review.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian military and judicial institutions under el-Sisi's government, not a demonstrated personal order.","limitations":["The source does not give the total number of affected civilians."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":22,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported insufficient protection for human-rights defenders, opposition figures, civil-society activists, journalists, lawyers, trade unionists, scholars, students, bloggers and artists critical of the government, including threats, harassment, reprisals, prolonged pretrial detention, torture, enforced disappearance and denial of lawyer access.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","6B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"This institutional finding was issued in 2023 concerning the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns government protection and security practice under el-Sisi's presidency; it does not prove his personal direction of each act.","limitations":["The source aggregates reported patterns and does not identify every responsible agency or case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":23,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported high numbers of deaths, including violent deaths, in detention, allegations that torture and lack of health care frequently caused deaths, and a lack of reliable disaggregated data and information on investigations.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","6B.2","6B.5","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was made in the Committee's 2023 observations for the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns detention institutions under el-Sisi's government; personal responsibility is not directly established.","limitations":["The source supplies no total number of deaths or verified causal breakdown."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported that torture was routinely used to extract confessions, that such confessions were invoked in court against defendants, and that courts generally did not investigate related complaints despite constitutional and procedural guarantees.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Committee recorded this reported practice in its 2023 review of the period under review.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns police, prosecutors and courts under el-Sisi's government; it does not establish a personal presidential order.","limitations":["The document does not identify the number or outcome of individual complaints."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":24,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"The Committee found that Egypt's death-penalty framework covered many offences, including some not involving intentional killing, and reported a high and growing number of death sentences and executions, often in counter-terrorism cases lacking due process; it also reported allegations of death sentences based on coerced confessions, sentences against children for alleged pre-18 conduct and secret executions without timely family notification.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","4B.4","6B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The observations were adopted in 2023 and concern the legal and practical situation during the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian law and courts under el-Sisi's government; personal involvement in individual sentences is not shown.","limitations":["The source uses reported figures and allegations without a complete execution or sentencing dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":25,"end_unit":27,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported a high number of children aged 12 to 18 deprived of liberty during investigations despite statutory protections, and reports that detained children were tortured, held in solitary confinement, sometimes held with adults, recruited into armed violence in North Sinai and lacked information about their rights and abuse-reporting channels.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"This was a 2023 finding concerning treatment during the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian detention and security authorities under el-Sisi's presidency; it does not identify a personal presidential directive.","limitations":["The source gives no quantified number of affected children."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":28,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported that persons accused under prostitution law were sometimes subjected to forced anal examinations and that vaginal examinations were sometimes conducted without consent to prove sexual acts.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.7","4B.3"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was issued in 2023 concerning practices during the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian law-enforcement practice under el-Sisi's government; personal direction is not established.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the frequency of these examinations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":30,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"The Committee acknowledged that Egypt hosted a significant number of refugees and asylum-seekers but found no adequate asylum and non-refoulement legislative framework and reported border apprehension, detention, denial of asylum procedures and return of at-risk asylum-seekers, along with overcrowded detention and inadequate medical care.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","6B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The Committee made this finding in 2023 concerning the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian migration and asylum authorities under el-Sisi's government; personal responsibility is indirect.","limitations":["The document does not provide the number of people returned or detained."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":31,"end_unit":32,"fact_summary":"The Committee reported widespread gender-based violence against women and girls, no comprehensive law on gender-based violence, discriminatory criminal-code provisions, underreporting caused by stigma and fear, and low prosecution and conviction rates with lenient penalties.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was issued in 2023 concerning the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egypt's legal and enforcement institutions under el-Sisi's government; it does not establish his personal conduct.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the national incidence of gender-based violence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":31,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"The Committee welcomed Egypt's harsher penalties for female genital mutilation, the 2022-2026 eradication plan and the national committee, but found the practice remained prevalent, reporting 86 percent prevalence among women aged 15-49, especially in rural and remote areas, along with underreporting, low prosecution and continued impunity.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The institutional finding was adopted in 2023 and includes the latest prevalence figure cited in the supplied text.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns state policy and implementation under el-Sisi's government; personal authorship of the plan is not established.","limitations":["The supplied extraction contains encoding corruption around the percentage but clearly states 86 percent."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aee8a9c7557ca955","start_unit":34,"end_unit":35,"fact_summary":"The Committee welcomed Egypt's anti-trafficking law, 2022-2026 national strategy and coordinating committee, but found persistent trafficking of women migrant workers and children, inadequate enforcement, incomplete operation of referral and victim-assistance funds, and low prosecution and conviction rates.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The Committee recorded these findings in 2023 concerning implementation during the review period.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns Egyptian anti-trafficking institutions under el-Sisi's government; personal responsibility is not directly shown.","limitations":["The source
